properties.name: A held-design test waits for its holder's own word, not a read that can take the store first
properties.rationale:
OBSERVED: "the --serve-shared server never took the store" at hold(), a different case of the six each time, on CI for main 72bf252 (run 37110378324), PR #660 and PR #661, each after about 80 s; the file passed on main 230008c and 293f957 and on reruns. Findings: fact:a-held-design-test-flakes-waiting-30s-for-the-holder-to-take-the-store-2026-10-03 (item 6, cause not established) and fact:a-held-design-test-fails-in-ci-because-the-shared-server-never-took-the-store-2026-10-03 (item 7a, cause measured with a replica, 2 of 20).

THE CAUSE, measured here independently (root-cause skill, fetched fresh): hold() spawned the holder and at once began probing with `--call get_node` every 100 ms until a probe's stderr said SNAPSHOT. On a store nobody holds yet, that read opens the real store and takes its lock for the whole call (about 0.4 s; strace: the probe takes the lock ~340 ms after exec, the holder ~230 ms after its exec, so the holder normally wins by ~100 ms). When the holder started late enough to lose that margin, it found the lock taken and exited with "not becoming the shared server ... the store lock picks one winner and the rest exit here" - by design, since a --serve-shared server is spawned by a session that attaches to the winner; here nothing respawns it. Every later probe then opened the store itself (exit 0, no SNAPSHOT) until the 300th. A replica of the loop with the holder's stderr kept failed 2 of 30 times on a loaded 4-core box and 1 of 40 in a second, interleaved round, each time with 300 direct opens, the holder dead, and that sentence in its log; the same replica waiting for the rendezvous first failed 0 of 40 in that interleaved round. Those counts alone do not separate the two waits (3 of 70 against 0 of 40); the holder's log and the deterministic pin do. CANDIDATES REFUTED by that log: a holder that crashed or refused for another reason (it said lost race, not REFUSING), a copy that failed (no probe printed SNAPSHOT), a probe budget too short (300 probes ran for ~80 s).

THE CLASS is a readiness wait that competes for the resource it waits to see held. Swept: every test that starts a holder (--serve-shared, --http, stdio) and then probes. --http servers and --shared clients recover from a lost lock (degraded serving retries; clients respawn), and the tests that start them wait for the listening line or a client's own handshake. The one other wait that probed by opening the store was a_build_can_call_one_tool_from_the_shell.rs's held test: a WRITE through --call against a stdio holder, which could write into the design and leave the holder degraded until a retry fell between probes; it now waits for the holder's answer to initialize (a holder that found the store taken says UNAVAILABLE there). The pin starts the holder 1.5 s late through sh and asserts no --call runs before the holder has published: the old loop failed it 6 of 6 times (5 early calls each); it passes now.

NOT CHANGED, and why: the product behaviour. A --serve-shared server that loses the lock exits by design, and a one-shot --call opening the store is the documented single-writer door; whether --call should reach a running server instead is open as dec:idea-a-one-shot-call-reaches-the-design-where-it-is-served. NOT MEASURED: the fixed file on CI more than this PR's own runs.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: hold() in a_held_designs_read_is_as_true_as_the_live_one.rs waits for the --serve-shared holder's rendezvous to name its pid (written only once the server holds the store and its port is bound; reading it opens nothing), fails at once with the holder's own stderr if the holder exits first, then checks once that a read through the door answers from a copy. a_holder_that_starts_late_is_waited_for_without_being_raced pins it. a_build_can_call_one_tool_from_the_shell.rs's held test waits for its stdio holder's answer to initialize instead of probing with a write. Test code only; no product change.
